sections.heading: C - Motorcycles, Pedestrians, and School Buses
sections.markdown:
## C - Motorcycles, Pedestrians, and School Buses

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Scan for motorcycles and look closely before entering any intersection or changing lanes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
A bike's small profile fools depth perception, so it often looks much farther off than it truly is [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Never tailgate a motorcycle, since it can halt faster than surrounding cars [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Riders frequently slow by downshifting or easing the throttle, which never lights the brake lamp [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Never squeeze past a rider with only feet to spare, because the wind blast can throw the bike down [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
When a motorcycle overtakes you, hold your lane position and never accelerate [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Keep more than a 4-second gap behind motorcycles, widening it for foul weather, gusts, wet or icy pavement, potholes, gravel, and rail crossings [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
Always flash turn signals before lane changes, among the most protective acts for nearby riders [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
Driver-assist systems may miss motorcycles entirely, so watch your surroundings and honor every tip above [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A01
Operating a motorcycle or moped on a public road requires age 16 or older [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A01
Riders under 18 must carry a learner license for 12 months with zero moving-violation convictions before earning a Motorcycle Only license [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A01
Motorcycle operators must finish an approved safety course plus hold a license endorsement or a Motorcycle Only license [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A01
Moped operators need a Class E driver license, with no motorcycle endorsement demanded [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A01
Helmets stay mandatory for riders under 21; riders 21 or older may skip one only while carrying medical insurance paying at least $10,000 for injuries [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A01
Motorcycle and moped operators need not carry Personal Injury Protection insurance [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A01
Bikes and mopeds need yearly registration with the right tag and must stay off bicycle and foot paths [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A01
Motorists must do everything possible to avoid striking walkers, and riders on bikes, skateboards, or skates count as pedestrians inside crosswalks and driveways [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Halt and stay halted for pedestrians crossing any street or driveway at marked crossings and intersections [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
Stop for sidewalk pedestrians whenever entering or leaving alleys, driveways, and private roads [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Never clog a crosswalk at a red light or let any part of your car hang over it [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
Never overtake a car stopped at a crosswalk for a walker; always assume someone may be crossing even when nobody shows [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
Stop fully before every right on red and scan both directions for crosswalk pedestrians [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A02
Stop completely, yield, and take extra care around blind pedestrians with white canes tipped red or service animals, mobility-impaired people with walkers, crutches, orthopedic canes, wheelchairs, or guide dogs, and children or confused or incapacitated walkers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A02
Walkers must leave the roadway whenever a sidewalk exists [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A02
Without a sidewalk, walk the left shoulder facing oncoming traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A02
Cross at intersections or marked crosswalks, noting intersection crosswalks may be marked or unmarked [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A02
Outside a crosswalk, pedestrians yield the right-of-way to vehicles [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A02
Walkers yield to vehicles in the crosswalk whenever the signal glows red or reads DON’T WALK [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A02
Stay out from between parked cars, pause at the curb to look left, right, then left again, wear bright reflective neon and carry a flashlight after dark, and skip texting and headphones [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A02
Yield to same-direction transit buses signaling their return to traffic from signed pullout bays [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A03
Passing a school bus flashing its stop signal breaks the law [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A03
On undivided two-way roads, traffic in both directions stops for a bus loading or unloading children and waits until the signal drops and every child clears the road [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A03
Opposite-direction drivers skip the stop only past a raised barrier or unpaved median at least 5 feet wide, since painted lines never qualify, while same-direction drivers always stop until the signal drops [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A03
Honor school zones, signs, and crossing guards who enter first and leave last, and stop at the stop line rather than inside the crosswalk when children or guards occupy it [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A03
Farm rigs built under 25 MPH must show the slow-vehicle emblem on the rear on public highways outside interstates and run daylight-only without proper night lamps and reflectors [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A03
Paved-across two-lane and multi-lane roads order both directions to stop, while divided highways order only traffic behind the bus to stop and let opposite traffic proceed cautiously [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0097]
